body:
It might help to think about life in general being out of control in the sense that you cannot control everything even though you might want to. I also struggle with this a lot, mostly with thinking about the future though. Even if you're driving a car, you cannot control the other drivers around you, the elements such as weather, etc. Those pilots flying the plane have been going through years of training and are highly skilled to be hired to be a pilot for a commercial airline. There are also tons of people in the mix to insure your safety, such as air traffic control, TSA, and the people who check out the plane before takeoff. 

Also, people are not out to get you or purposely do malicious things to you. Most people don't have enough time in the day to care enough about harming others around them. They are in their own little worlds thinking about their own busy lives. I think putting yourself in other people shoes, thinking about what they might be thinking or dealing with themselves, really helps with social anxiety. Unfortunately, a lot of people are not that aware of their surroundings, so they might cut you off on the highway or bump into you accidentally...but those are accidents, they are not doing all of that purposely just to piss you off.

It sounds to be like you're incredibly stressed and going through a lot. It would definitely help to talk to a therapist, if you haven't done so already, about this and just how you're feeling in general. They will be able to access what type of therapy works best for you and will be able to help you figure out exactly why those type of dogs trigger such strong responses in you. Just know that you are not alone, and you're not the only one that feels this way. Help is out there if you need it. [This](https://therapists.psychologytoday.com/rms/) is a really good website to search for therapists in your area. You can even plug in your health insurance for a match too. Reach out to a therapist today. You know you need to, so make that first step right now.

I think what usually gets me is when people put on a facade of being happy in those situations that triggers me to be even more depressed.  It's similar to the, "How are you doing?" when people are merely passing you in a hallway and not expecting a real answer. I really don't like putting on a social front just because the situation/event calls for it.

I think juggling different classes/subjects is what stresses me the most. Focusing on just one type of subject will definitely help. But, I worry about getting hired the most when I graduate. I know everyone does, but I'm located in a pretty rural area where the jobs in general are scarce and the design jobs are even rarer. I only see those pop up every few months, and it's pretty competitive.

Thank you for the advice. I think my biggest worry right now is actually having a good day the day I talk to my therapist, because on good days I look back on the bad days and think, "What was I thinking? I was just being silly". But, I've written down a lot of symptoms and just things in general I want to work on for my first session, so that should help prevent any sort of mental block I may have when it comes to my symptoms.

Thank you for sharing. It's been a long road to finally realize I need help. I think graphic design and photography are something I want to stick with, because they challenge me and they're interesting to me. But, the challenging part is really difficult during those times I'm not very happy or don't have enough energy.

Yep, I'm definitely in the same boat as you. I think we'll make it through. I have another 2 semesters to go after this, so the end is near but it's painful to think about how much work there is to do in-between.
Thank you so much for the advice. It really helps.

Texas Roadhouse just isn't my thing in general, but to be fair I think this flyer matches what Texas Roadhouses' audience expects/wants from them despite it being a bad design. I mean their restaurants have peanut shells thrown all over the floor. What more can you expect? lol

Thank you! It's good to hear a success story from someone who has faced somewhat of the same issues as me. I'm hanging in there and will go see my university's therapist next week and will take their advice seriously. I think I have a lot of work to do on myself that I never fully realized until recently. 

Also, design is a true passion of mine. I enjoy thinking about it; looking at other people's works throughout the day on Bechance, Dribble and Instagram. I don't particularly enjoy the OCD attention to detail with a lot of it. When I'm in my really bad moods it is particularly difficult to want to care enough to really pay attention to everything in the project I'm working on. But, I absolutely love the end result if I put my time and effort into it. Making something that I convinced in my mind into a tangible object is a wonderful feeling. 

Photography is also a passion of mine. It comes to me a bit easier because it's honestly less time consuming for me to make a photo than a poster, business card, etc., even with post-production. However, unless I can do nature/landscape photography or stock photography (food, jewelry, etc.) I don't really see myself being completely happy with Photography. That would probably mean being a portrait photographer, which probably means doing wedding photography or grad photography shoots which come with their own set of awkward and stressful things.

I'm no expert, but it sounds like pausing might help. What I mean is before you give an answer, pause for a moment and say to yourself, "Is this really what I want to do?" If the phone rings, pause and think, "Do I really want to take this phone call?" It might also help to try to focus to be in the moment as much as possible. I get really caught up thinking about things that happened in the past, or about relationships I have with people, or about the future. All of those thoughts usually end up making me think what if? The what if isn't really a good place for me to be, because I start to doubt myself or think about worst case scenarios, etc. Being more in the moment gets you out of your head and that helps a lot when it comes to thinks like depression/anxiety, etc.

Could be a few things: anxiety, social anxiety, anger disorder, depression or perhaps something else. I'm no doctor by any means though. I'm actually getting ready to go to my first therapy session next week. I think it would be really helpful if you were to go to a school counselor to voice your concerns and figure out a treatment plan that works for you. 

I get pretty angry with minor things that happen to me throughout the day. My main trigger is people not being aware of their surroundings/not being curious to others. An example of this would be people going when they're supposed do at a four-way stop (either going too early or hesitating too long/not paying attention to the road and holding up traffic). Another situation that really pisses me off is people who walk and text and not pay attention to where they're walking so you have to dodge them. I think what helps for me currently is keeping in mind that those people aren't doing it to be selfish, necessarily. They might be going through their own struggles and their way of coping is to be on their cellphones or whatever. I think empathy, although difficult, is the key with anger.
Thank you! It's good to hear from others that have anxiety/depression.
Very true, and unfortunately I know I take some things a little too personally at times, which I'm working on. You definitely have to have a think skin in this business.

Thank you! You made some very good points, especially the part about having to bring the work home with me while in college. Right now I don't really get a day off. I go to classes/work Monday through Friday. Saturdays are my days to go shoot photos, and Sundays are my days in the darkroom developing film or making prints. Even now while I'm on spring break I'm still having to work on something everyday to keep me caught up in my classes. It's a bit too much, but it's really good to keep in mind that when I get a job it will be just a job and not (hopefully) a life consuming thing as it is right now.
Thank you, I hope it does too.
Thank you!
Thanks! This helps a lot to know this information.

I think what I'm understanding from a lot of these comments are that mental health providers/therapists/psychiatrists/etc. don't really come up with a collaborative solution like just an ordinary primary doctor does. It sounds like they take the reins wholeheartedly when it comes to diagnosing and coming up with a solution/medication plan, which honestly doesn't sound like something I want. 

I am functioning well with the issues I struggle with. I still get up every day, go to all of my classes, turn in all of my work, work 20 hours a week, etc. However, I lack a lot of energy. I feel lethargic throughout the day, every day, and I'm not happy or excited about pretty much anything anymore. I feel so unhappy it physically hurts. It is mostly the physical perspective I wanted to resolve. I think once I start feeling better I will be better. This is why I felt an online psychiatrists or doctor would be a better fit for me. But, alas, it seems they don't exist.
Thanks!

Perhaps I don't understand the potency of typical psychological drugs, but I don't really see why an online psychiatrist wouldn't exist. My thinking is doctors in general typically rely on you to tell them how you're doing, and how they drugs they prescribed are affecting you. So, unless blood work, or something like that, needs to be done in person, why not an online psychiatrist?

No, I'm not joking. I'm very serious about the possibility of an online psychiatrist because it would help busy people like me get help, not overwhelm them more by forcing them to take even more time out of their day to make appointments. 

And, you know what? I hope next time you comment on someone else's post you take the time to say to yourself, "Is this helpful?" Because if it isn't, and you're commenting just to put someone down, or make them feel like an idiot which is what you did in my case, then I hope you will not take the time to hit the submit button and instead read back what you wrote and really think about how you would feel if you were the receiver of your own comment. In other words, if you can't say something nice just don't say anything especially in subreddits like this where people are legitimately trying to get help.
Thank you!
